item.title: Scandinavians, look here! - The Scandinavian Branch (ND) seeks recruits!
item.description: Recruitment thread for the Scandinavian Branch (ND).
item.content:encoded:
Hello!

We in the Scandinavian branch (ND) of the SCP Foundation are looking for new members. If you happen to speak Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, or even Faroese, you are more than welcome to come join the ND Wiki and the ND Discord server!

Because the ND branch is still in need of further development, we're especially interested in people with experience in any of the following areas:
- Moderation and Administration
- CSS coding and other technical know-how
- Translation
- Creative writing in Danish, Faroese, Norwegian, and/or Swedish

If you have experience in the two first areas (in addition to speaking one of the four languages) and wish to apply that knowledge in ND, please contact me directly with a short resume of your experiences.

Of course you're welcome as a member even if you don't already have a background in any of these areas. We need all the help we can get.
So if you're interested, come on over to http://scp-nd.wikidot.com/ and sign up!
You're also welcome to join our Discord server at: https://discord.gg/QTsMfgAu

item.title: That Halloween Spirit!
item.description: We've really gone for it this year.
item.content:encoded:
Most bone-chilling greetings to ye! I have returned from my absence to do my yearly Halloween round up, and this year I am most impressed.

The site is dressed up black and orange, the truest colours of Halloween (plus purple). No Halloween feature, but honestly the look is impressive enough to me. Insidious pumpkin face on the logo, serial killer font, Spook, Creep, Pester! I love it. Outside of the main site the Halloween spirit is strong as well. Google Translate still doesn't work for Chinese, so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯, but elsewhere it's in full force!
The German wiki keeps on giving as it does every year (makes sense I suppose, theirs is the home of the Grimm tales), having just ended another Halloween competition, with a great spooky theme to boot.
Sadly, the French didn't do anything this year, though they do have a neat competition on the theme of errors, with a very clever theme rearranging the widgets on the page.
The Italian branch is also having a Halloween contest. No special page theme, but they have found a way to implement a dark mode, which is nice (possible feature of Project Foundation?).
The Polish branch didn't want to be left out and have a competition of their own, with the interesting theme of articles that have previously been deleted (meta-zombies, anybody?). Ressurection of the Removed, Translate calls it.
And the Spanish-speaking branch, oh my, they have outdone themselves. Not just a cool page theme with an animated banner, not just some nice art on the main page, but a skeleton vs pumpkin story-fighting competition, where the two sides go head-to-head represented by gifs of a skeleton head and a pumpkin breathing fire at each other! Top marks.

Small notes about the other sites.
– hide block
  • The Brazilian branch has a neat theme, but it doesn't seem to be Halloween related. They also have an animated logo, where the SCP logo is the wheels of a car, which is… cool?
  • Why do the Russian and Ukrainian branches have different page layouts to everyone else?
  • In a funny example of Google Translate's imperfection, the Ukrainian version of 'Secure, Contain, Protect' has been translated to 'Protect, Hold, Protect'.

Back in the English-speaking part of the internet, we have social media.
YouTuber TheeSherm is putting on a 24-hour Halloween charity livestream again, live right now! He's gathered a bunch of SCP authors and creators and they'll be doing just SCP stuff for 24 hours, in aid of an LGBT centre. Details here.
I can't tell if the SCP subreddit is being especially spooky today, because honestly they're always like that. But the colours are especially black and orange today, so perhaps they did put in some extra effort.

That's all I have for you. If I missed anything, please comment it yourself. I leave you again with the Word of the Day. Today it's 'eldritch', but I'm sure most of you already know that word, being on this site and all, so instead I'll give you yesterday's, which is one of my favourite words ever: 'gloaming'.

Gloaming, noun: twilight, dusk, specifically the part of dusk where the sun has set but the sky is not completely dark as its glow is still visible on the horizon; 'The Gloaming Wildwoods'1.

Happy Halloween, and stay safe!

Footnotes
1. Many points if you get this reference

item.title: "Real" amnestics effect
item.content:encoded:
So, first off, amnestics as used in the wiki are basically magic for a variety of reasons (In short: memory doesn't work that way, real amnestics don't work that way, etc.)

However, I just learned an interesting little tidbit. See (by current understanding, anyway), information the is being encoded in long-term memory1 undergoes a consolidation period over hours or days, during which much of it is forgotten. The rest stays (relatively) stable. Actual amnestics make it harder to form memories after they have entered your system.

However, electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) causes difficulty in remembering things that happen recently before the therapy and causes difficulty forming new memories for a bit after, basically disrupting consolidation.

Now, older memories tend to be resistant to this effect. However, if you ask them to remember an older memory shortly before ECT, the older memory is subject to degradation as well.

So, if you interrogate someone deeply about a past event or facts and then give them ECT, you could mess with that info.

It's not guaranteed to impact what you want it to (or to impact memory at all), and it's not the fancy "rewind and delete" or "target a specific date range" wiki version, but it's apparently real.

Footnotes
1. which is for the most part any info longer than about 2 minutes ago

item.title: The SCP Halloween Playlist
item.description: A playlist of our favorite Halloween-y songs!
item.content:encoded:
Hello SCPeople,

In this thread, everyone can chip in a few of their favorite songs that they associate with Halloween or Autumn, along with a small prompt about why they're your favorite. Then, when the big day rolls around, I'll make a playlist of everybody's songs and a document with all of your prompts. I'm not aware that something like this has been done before, and I think it can be a fun way to take a snapshot of the SCP community and its inhabitants as we are now!

It's very simple in concept, but of course we could make it as fancy and fun as we want!
As far as what kinds of songs are allowed, there are basically no rules - anything from your favorite black metal dirge to a song you remember listening to on Halloween night as kid. You can even get memey with it, if you so choose! I only ask that if there are dark themes in the song, you provide appropriate Trigger Warnings. Since I'm sure some of you have a hundred spooky songs that you love (this being the SCP wiki) I'd like to keep it to a limit of 3 songs per person. After a few people have contributed, I'll give my own songs :>

Everyone should feel free to comment on other people's choices, strike up discussions, and compliment each others taste - just keep it positive!

Everyone have fun, and enjoy the longer nights, the falling leaves, and the howling in the woods!

(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MarBVyZVe9s)

item.title: The SCP "Canon": What articles on the site have lasting artistic value?
item.description: Articles that transcend their wiki boundaries to having "literary" merit.
item.content:encoded:
The SCP Wiki, while perhaps not meant to be a bastion of quality as much as an incubator for talent or a simple free-for-all writing arena, has certainly produced works that many would claim are "better" or "of higher value" than the rest. Objectively speaking, thousands of articles kick 682 to the curb.

If this is the case, what articles on the wiki exceed expectations and possess value and merit that could be appreciated for years or even decades to come, past the SCP Wiki, to become "literature"?

Of course, some rules:

  • What is viewed as having literary merit in the modern world doesn't always relate to a work's quality, nor is it stagnant. This is why I put "literature", and especially the word "canon", in quotes. However, certain stories possess masterful prose, engaging characters, insightful perspectives, and timeless themes, wrapped in an author's bow. These are works that can be enjoyed and analyzed for eons without losing their touch. That's what is being sought here; something you could see being taught in an English class, separated from its Wiki context.
  • One may say that articles on the SCP wiki do require its wiki context, which is fair when talking about a lot of articles. However, 173 managed immense world-building in under 500 words and, most of all, developed the Foundation into a character before the Foundation even existed. Good articles on the SCP wiki do this as well, while great articles do this and then some. This is not to say that articles of lasting artistic merit can't call back on or reference other works of fiction, including other articles on the wiki. However, the article should be enjoyed on its own merits, with greater understanding of the context enhancing the article's value.
  • In essence, this is no different than a "what are the best articles on the site" question, but what I want to do, as I've said previously, is generate a list of works that could be shown to someone who doesn't know what the SCP wiki is and have them still appreciate it. There are some articles on this site that work well as SCP wiki articles, but perhaps not as separated fiction as a whole.
  • Every articles deserves to be appreciated in some way, and just because it isn't remembered or appreciated doesn't mean it's bad, not by any means. But this solely concerns articles that you believe could be appreciated for years to come.
  • I should note that by "articles", I mean SCP entries (including -Js and -EXs), tales, and GoI-formats. Just so we're clear.
